title: Document the framework-vs-current-project skill convention in routing + CLAUDE.md
description: Teach the orchestrator and future contributors the two-variant convention introduced by TASK-153/154 so the right skill is picked in each context. Update: (1) .claude/skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md — a short subsection noting that hive-self-improve / hive-adversarial-improve / hivemind-assimilate-skill are FRAMEWORK-repo-only, and their -current-project counterparts (hive-self-improve-current-project, hive-adversarial-improve-current-project, assimilate-current-project) are the CONSUMER-project entry points, gated by isFrameworkRepo (src/framework-context.js). (2) CLAUDE.md — a brief pointer in the Knowledge Sharing or Workflow area to the same convention. Keep it terse; the skills themselves carry the operational detail. uat-only: pure docs, no code; verify via a short UAT script that a reader can tell which variant to invoke from which context. If any doc-lock sensor guards these files, keep it green.
acceptance_criteria: orchestrator-routing SKILL.md explains the framework vs -current-project variant split and names isFrameworkRepo as the gate
CLAUDE.md carries a brief pointer to the convention (which skills are framework-only vs consumer-facing)
Docs name all six skills correctly and match the actual shipped/relocated layout from TASK-153/154
Any doc-lock/parity sensor over these files stays green; npm test green
UAT: from the docs alone, a reader correctly picks hive-self-improve in the framework repo and hive-self-improve-current-project in a consumer project
